CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Overview

This is an R package called markermd that provides a Shiny-based interface for grading assignments submitted as git repositories containing Quarto (.qmd) documents. The package includes template creation functionality and validation rule systems for automated grading workflows. Document parsing is built on the q2r package; the legacy parsermd dependency has been removed. Quarto .qmd is the primary format; .Rmd documents are read the same way (knitr chunk headers are normalized before parsing, see use_qmd).

Development Commands

When you’re running package tests, use devtools::load_all(); testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/path-to-file.R"). The shinytest2 (browser) tests call skip_on_cran(), so a single-file run needs NOT_CRAN=true in the environment (for example NOT_CRAN=true Rscript -e 'devtools::load_all(); testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-mark-grading.R")'); without it every browser block reports a skip and the run looks green. devtools::test() sets it for you. Setting MARKERMD_SKIP_BROWSER_TESTS=true skips every browser test (the check lives in new_app_driver()); the R-CMD-check GitHub workflow sets it, and the browser tests run in .github/workflows/browser-tests.yaml, started by hand (gh workflow run browser-tests.yaml). If that doesn’t work don’t delete tests that otherwise should work, instead ask me what to do.

To run all tests in the package use devtools::test().

After making changes to any R or C++ files, one of these commands must be run: - devtools::load_all() - Fast rebuild for the current R session only. Use for quick testing and iterative development. Changes are only visible in the current session. - devtools::install() - Slower but persistent installation. Updates the package for all future R sessions. Required when changes need to be available system-wide.

Architecture

The package is designed around two main interfaces:

Core Functions

  • mark() - launches the main grading application for collections of student repositories
  • template() - launches the template creation application for single assignments
  • Git operations: Uses gert package for all git interactions
  • Document parsing: Uses the q2r package to parse qmd files into a Pandoc AST. Knitr-style chunk headers ({r label, opts}) are rewritten to Quarto #| form by normalize_knitr_chunks() before parsing, since q2r/pampa rejects them (error Q-2-36); the rewrite returns a line_map attribute (the file line of each parsed line) that parse_assignment_document() uses to add an “is line N of the file” hint to any diagnostic whose line moved, and that the Grade tab’s Source view uses (map_ranges_to_original()) to highlight the file as written. mark() parses one document per repository, chosen by find_repo_assignment() like validate_project() and parse_project() (parse_repo_documents()), never the first qmd found anywhere in the repo
  • UI framework: Modern Shiny app using bslib for layout and styling

Application Architecture

  1. Template Creation Interface (template() function):
    • Interactive AST tree visualization for document structure exploration
    • Question-based organization system with node selection capabilities
    • Validation rule system for each question with multiple rule types
    • S7 class-based state management for questions and rules
    • Template saving/loading functionality
  2. Grading Interface (mark() function):
    • Collection-based workflow for multiple student repositories
    • Template-driven validation and scoring
    • Repository comparison and navigation
    • Validation result visualization
    • Five tabs: Assignments (the landing page; one per-repository table with the repo’s links, validation status, grading progress, per-question scores and total, and the class summary pinned beneath as column footers), Grade (grading: the content pane beside the current question’s rubric; tab value grade), Rubric (every question’s rubric edited in one place, tab value rubric: mark_rubric_editor_ui() and output$rubric_editor_ui in the same rubric module, so both tabs share its item, group and grade servers; each item shows its selection count (item_selection_counts()) in place of its toggle and each question’s scoring inputs come from mark_grade_settings_ui(), with the same ids as the grade widget’s popovers. Both tabs draw the rubric from the same handles under their own id prefixes (rubric_module-grade-..., rubric_module-editor-...; rx$view_id()), so both can be on the page at once; each view redraws on structural changes and when its tab is entered, and the editor is drawn only while the Rubric tab is shown; the Rubric tab’s scoring inputs are the grade widget’s with an editor_ prefix (mark_grade_settings_ui()) and the grade server saves either set; add_item_to() / add_group_to() take the question; a question’s handles are built lazily by ensure_question_loaded() the first time it is shown, the Rubric tab opens, or something is added to it; new item and group ids are minted above used_item_ids() plus the ids in memory (rx$new_ids()); the Rubric tab header has its own YAML import / export controls, editor_import_file and editor_export_all, sharing the Grade tab’s handler), History (one timeline of the project’s snapshots and its activity log, filtered by kind; see mod_mark_history.R, whose history_timeline_rows() merges activity_rows() into the snapshot rows; the timeline takes the full width and a click on a row (reactable onClick, reported to open_entry) opens the entry’s detail in an xl modal, which branches on selected_id() (a snapshot, with pin / restore / export / delete in its header; the restore, export and delete dialogs have a Back button to the detail) versus selected_activity() (an activity entry, with a Snapshot before button)), an optional Terminal tab (mark(terminal = TRUE) or a named list of commands; a shinyterm tabset, from Suggests, whose “+” menu starts a shell, claude or codex in the project root, see mod_mark_terminal.R), plus a navbar status link showing, on two lines beside a camera, the selection events recorded since the latest snapshot and its age. The app-wide repo selection is changed only through the select_repo() helper in mark-app.R; the table’s score cells (which open the repo and question in the Grade tab) and the rubric’s navigation sync go through it. The table’s validation marker instead opens a modal with that repo’s rule results (show_validation_modal(), which does not move the app-wide selection): the validate module’s cards plus a question shortcut select in the modal header, and a Re-check button that re-parses and re-validates that one repository (recheck_repo(), which updates the collection_rv / validation_rv / errors_rv reactive values every display reads, so a submission repaired while the app is open shows its new state), namespaced to the validate module, whose labels carry a coloured ✓/✗ via a selectize render function and which scrolls to the question’s card through the markermd_scroll_to custom message, expanding it first if collapsed. The module’s script lives once in the page head (mark_validate_script()); each card’s header carries its status and rule results and its body (the matched content) is a Bootstrap collapse, collapsed by default; the expanded question names are reported to the module’s expanded_questions input, which the render reads under isolate() so a later opening keeps the same cards expanded. The shortcut select starts empty (a placeholder) on every opening, so only an actual choice scrolls. validation_shown is bumped on each opening so the results render into the new modal DOM, and a node preview (which replaces the modal) has a Back button that re-opens it. Repository names in the table are plain text, not buttons.

Input Handling

template() accepts any of: an initialized markermd project directory (authors against the project’s key repo, preloads the template stored in the project database, and saves edits back into that database), a path to an assignment file (.qmd/.Rmd), a directory containing one (matched by the filename glob), a saved template (.yaml/.yml), an in-memory markermd_template, or a GitHub <owner>/<repo> (cloned into local_dir). mark() takes an initialized markermd project directory (one containing .markermd/config.yml; see init_project()) and sources everything from that config: student repos under the configured repos/ dir, the grading template (stored in the DB), the SQLite DB at <root>/.markermd/markermd.sqlite, and per-repo rendered HTML reports (“artifacts”) resolved from the configured artifacts: directories (resolve_repo_artifacts() in utils_artifacts.R). An optional template argument (object or .yaml path) overrides the stored one. The grading template is stored in the project’s SQLite database (the canonical store), as a JSON blob under the metadata table’s template key; YAML is an optional import/export format via template_import() / template_export() (the converters live in R/template-serialization.R, validated against the JSON Schema in inst/schema/markermd-template.json). The assignment document is referenced by source.path (a relative path resolves against the enclosing project root first, enclosing_project_root(), then the template file’s directory, then the working directory) and re-parsed on load to regenerate the AST, which is never stored. Bad inputs raise specific, actionable errors, and loading a template whose format_version predates the current markermd_template_version() errors with a message to recreate it.

Coding Style

  • Assignment operator: Always use = for assignment, never <-
  • Package dependencies: Always use explicit namespace prefixing (e.g., q2r::parse_qmd(), gert::git_clone()) rather than importing functions
  • String construction: Prefer glue::glue() over paste() or paste0() for constructing long text strings, especially when building HTML, CSS, or other formatted content. In this case long strings should only be multiline strings or strings with multiple variables being inserted.
  • Glue templates: When using glue::glue() to generate CSS or JavaScript code, always use << and >> as delimiters (.open = "<<", .close = ">>") instead of the default { and } to avoid conflicts with JavaScript/CSS syntax and confusion with brace escaping.
  • Documentation: Do not use roxygen style function documentation for non-exported functions - internal functions can have comments documenting their usage and parameters but this should not be done using roxygen style comments as this results in Rd files that are not wanted as part of the package.

Documentation Style for Non-Exported Functions

Internal functions should use regular comments (not roxygen) with this format:

# Brief description of what the function does
#
# parameter1: Description of parameter1
# parameter2: Description of parameter2

function_name = function(parameter1, parameter2) {
  # function body
}

Key formatting rules: - Start with a brief description using regular # comments - Include an empty comment line # between description and parameters - Format parameters as # parameter_name: Description - Include an empty line between comments and function definition - No function title line needed - No @return documentation needed

Project Structure

  • Standard R package structure with .Rproj file
  • Uses roxygen2 for documentation (markdown enabled)
  • S7 class system for core data structures (markermd_question, markermd_rule, markermd_template, markermd_grade_state, markermd_rubric_item, markermd_project, etc.) defined in template-classes.R / rule-classes.R / project-classes.R
  • Modular Shiny architecture with separate UI/server modules for reusable components
  • Applications: template-app.R (the template() app, which runs the app built by the internal template_app() (input resolution), which resolves its source with resolve_assignment_source() (shared with assignment_outline()) over template_editor_app() (the editor itself); its save/dirty-tracking/import/export block lives in template-persistence.R as the plain wiring function template_persistence(), deliberately not a module so its ids stay in the app’s root namespace) and mark-app.R (the mark() app; mark_app() builds and returns the app object without running it, so it can be tested, as template_app() does for template())
  • Template-side modules: mod_ast.R (the ast_module_ui()/ast_module_server() AST tree module, plus the shared ast_preview_observers() preview-modal wiring; the template tree is rendered once per document, its highlight is patched in place by the markermd_tree_state message from tree_selection_state() whenever the active question’s deduplicated selection or filtered set changes, and every heading toggle and preview click reaches the server through the one delegated tree_event input (head script ast_tree_script())), mod_question.R (questions; its rules and filters row machines are the structural twins question_rules_server() in mod_question_rules.R and question_filters_server() in mod_question_filters.R, plain wiring functions sharing the dynamic-row helpers in mod_question_rows.R: make_render_trigger(), make_seen_registry(), sync_keyed_observers()), mod_rule.R / mod_filter.R (pure UI builders for the rule rows and filter groups; all input handling lives in the row machines)
  • Grading-side modules: mod_mark_rubric.R / mod_mark_rubric_item.R / mod_mark_rubric_group.R (rubric; the item list renders as blocks, each an ungrouped item or a group header wrapping its member rows, and mark_rubric_server() builds the shared context rx and calls the plain wiring functions rubric_state_wiring(), rubric_actions_wiring(), rubric_persistence_wiring() and rubric_views_wiring() (mod_mark_rubric_{state,actions,persist,views}.R); groups, like items, have no module servers: each is a rubric_group_handle(), and its move buttons, settings fields and Ungroup are reported by rubric_groups_js() to the module’s single group_event input as {group, action, value}, validated and saved in edit_group(), with header and settings patches sent to both views (markermd_update_group, markermd_group_feedback). Items have no module servers: each is a rubric_item_handle() (a reactive state holder) in question_item_servers, the rows are plain markup whose clicks and edits one delegated script in the page head (rubric_item_editing_head()) reports to the module’s single item_event input as {item, action, value} (descriptions on blur or after a pause, never per keystroke), routed by the container attributes from rubric_item_container_attrs(), and the Grade tab’s toggle buttons and agent badges are patched in place by the markermd_item_buttons / markermd_agent_badges messages; a row’s group menu is built when it opens from its container’s data-groups list. A toggle writes its grade rows (and an exclusive group’s sibling deselections) at once in toggle_item(); loading a pair’s stored selections (apply_saved_selections()) never writes. Descriptions identify items in every exchange format, so a new item gets a unique placeholder description (“New item”, selected on focus), and a blank or duplicate edit is refused with the row put back (markermd_item_text). The module’s bulk operations (item and group add, edit and delete, rubric import) run through the app’s app_action() (a with_action() with actor "app"), so they are in the activity log and raise the reload banner in other sessions, while the session filters its own action ids out of the external-change watcher (note_own_action()). Tests drive items with the item_event() helper in helper-mark-fixture.R), mod_mark_grade.R (score entry, plus the cap badge and the score breakdown popover), mod_mark_validate.R (validation display), mod_mark_history.R (the History tab: the full-width timeline, the detail modal with its Overview / Changes / Scores tabs, and the take / restore / export / delete / backup actions; a restore calls the rubric module’s reload_from_db())
  • Reports (artifacts): student-rendered HTML is shown in sandboxed iframes without allow-same-origin (artifact_iframe() in utils_artifacts.R), so a report’s scripts run but cannot reach the app’s page, inputs or session; the Grade tab shows a served copy of the report with a <base> and the highlight script injected (artifact_frame_url() / artifact_frame_script()) and drives the question highlight by postMessage (markermd_frame_highlight).
  • Snapshots: snapshots.R (the snapshot layer: snapshot_write() is the conn-based writer every bulk change calls inside its own transaction via snapshot_before_change(), snapshot_payload() builds the three plain exchange documents from a connection, and the exported snapshot_*() API plus project_backup() and the markermd_snapshot S7 class live here) and snapshot-diff.R (diff_rubric() / diff_marks() / diff_scores() / diff_template() over plain lists, the markermd_snapshot_diff class and snapshot_diff()). Schema version 5 adds the tables snapshots, snapshot_blobs (content-addressed canonical JSON, gzip when smaller, shared by identical parts and garbage-collected), snapshot_parts, snapshot_notes (append-only) and snapshot_stats (cached per-pair scores with (total) rows). An automatic snapshot of an unchanged state is recorded as a trigger note on the latest snapshot instead of a new row. Diffs and restores match questions by the ids in each snapshot’s template part (question_name_map(), rename_side_questions()). The rubric part carries item and group ids (rubric_to_list(ids = TRUE)), dropped on export, so the diff matches reworded items; the template part drops the template’s metadata so a re-save is not a change. The marks part carries each pair’s selected item ids beside the descriptions (marks_data_from_conn(ids = TRUE), dropped on export by marks_without_ids()), so score_snapshot_parts() scores by id and a restore does not depend on descriptions being unique. snapshot_restore() writes the parts back in place by id (restore_rubric_conn() upserts the snapshot’s items and groups under their own ids and soft-deletes what the snapshot lacks and brings back soft-deleted items and groups the snapshot carries, with their kept grade rows, so every repository’s selections of a surviving item are kept; restore_marks_conn() matches selections by item id) in one transaction, after a pre-restore snapshot; without repo every project repository is restored (pairs graded after the snapshot are cleared), with repo the other repositories are left alone, and the recomputed scores of the restored repositories must equal the snapshot’s cached ones or it aborts. The History tab’s restore goes through snapshot_restore_action() with actor "app", so it is in the activity log. export_scores() / export_comments() record an export note on the snapshot of the exported state. The *_import() functions take snapshot and summary arguments, the *_export() functions a snapshot argument.
  • Multi-file templates (template format 3.2): markermd_template@files lists the assignment’s other files (repository-relative paths, checked by template_file_path_problem()), and markermd_question@file names one of them (NA = the Quarto document). A question on a file (is_file_question()) covers the whole file: the S7 validators forbid node_ids, rules, filters and document scope on it, get_question_ast() returns an empty AST for it, and validate_repo_against_rules(ast, template, repo_dir) gives it validate_file_question()’s result (pass when find_repo_file() finds the path, else a same-named file anywhere in the repo). utils_files.R holds those plus file_view_ui() (the source in a code view, an image preview or a binary note), shared by the mark content pane (which shows a file question’s file whatever the html toggle says) and the template editor; assignment_file_candidates() lists the files under assignment_files_root() (the key directory, else the enclosing git repository, else the document’s directory; the one root template() and assignment_outline() share) with the default filters (hidden, render output, lock files, project files, README) for the Add files modal and assignment_outline()’s "files" attribute. In template(), template-files.R holds template_files_button_ui() (the Files button in the Questions card’s title bar), template_files_pane_ui() (the left pane: the document tree, or the active entry’s file through file_view_ui(), switched by conditional panels on the hidden template_shown_file text output) and template_files_server() (a plain wiring function like template_persistence(): the file view and the Add files modal; removing a file a question covers is refused). “Add Question” opens a modal (new_entry_name, new_entry_file from question_file_choices(), the document first under its own name, and new_entry_coverage on the document, confirmed by confirm_add_entry; a blank name takes default_question_name(), a taken one is refused). A question’s file and coverage are fixed once added: question_ui() shows the file as a read-only label beside the name (file_label) and has no body for a question on another file. Whole-file entries (document scope or another file) summarize as “Entire document”. Tests add questions through the add_entry() helper (helper-template-entry.R). The format version is 3.2 only when files is non-empty.
  • Activity log: actions.R (schema version 6). Every exported function that changes grading state (marks_import(), marks_set(), rubric_import(), rubric_item_set(), its bulk form rubric_items_set(), rubric_item_delete() (which asks before deleting a selected item, or needs force = TRUE outside an interactive session), template_import(), project_set(template = ...), snapshot_restore()) and every bulk operation of mark() (actor "app") runs its write inside with_action(), which stamps the action_id column of every grades / comments / private_comments row written meanwhile (via current_action_id() in the insert_*() helpers) and then writes one actions row (actor from markermd_actor(): MARKERMD_ACTOR, else CLAUDECODE -> claude, Codex’s sandbox variables -> codex, else R; the call, summary, a JSON scope, and the pre-change snapshot noted by snapshot_before_change()), plus the template / rubric before and after as action_parts rows into snapshot_blobs (kept by gc_snapshot_blobs()). A call that changed nothing records no row; nested calls belong to the outer one. App writes keep a NULL action_id and are grouped by idle gap (app_event_groups()). activity_rows() merges both, event_marks_diff() / activity_diff_conn() build an entry’s markermd_snapshot_diff, and the exported readers are project_activity() / activity_detail(). In mark(), watch_project_db() polls PRAGMA data_version on a later timer and bumps db_changed (it keeps its own connection, so the session’s own writes still change its data_version; it returns absorb(), which the app calls right after its own writes so they do not wake the external-change observer; a 30-second sweep still catches an outside commit landing in the same instant); an observer reads new actions rows, bumps external_version (which the table, History and the rubric badges depend on), shows one notification, calls the rubric module’s refresh_pair() (selections plus both comment boxes, keeping an unsaved edit) and, for a changed rubric or template, raises the external_change_banner (a rubric reload is a page reload, safe because each session now reads its rubric afresh; a template change needs a restart). pair_agent_badges() gives the items an action selected that no app write to the pair has followed; the rubric module patches them onto the Grade tab rows as a robot badge. The database runs in WAL mode. Schema version 9 soft-deletes rubric items and groups (deleted_at / deleted_action_id; migrate_item_soft_delete()): readers filter on live_item_sql, latest_rows() adds live_grade_item_sql for grades, deleting never removes grade rows so History is never rewritten, a deleted id is never reissued (used_item_ids(), reserved at startup by the rubric module), and group labels are unique only among live groups (partial index idx_item_groups_live_label). Schema version 8 adds the question id keys and the questions registry (a trigger fills question_id from the name for rows inserted without one). Schema version 7 writes the grading event tables’ timestamps in UTC ISO 8601 (event_timestamp(); parse_event_timestamp() reads both forms and migrate_event_timestamps() rewrites older rows). with_transaction() in utils_database.R is the one begin / commit / rollback wrapper every bulk writer uses. Inside an app session with_database() reuses the session’s connection (open_session_database(), called by both servers, keyed by session token and database path, closed on session end); outside one it opens its own. Transactions go through db_begin() / db_commit() / db_rollback(), which turn a nested begin into a savepoint.
  • Rubric item groups: a named, contiguous run of a question’s items whose combined points are clamped to an optional floor (<= 0) / ceiling (>= 0), or which is exclusive (at most one selected item; the app deselects the siblings on a user toggle, and marks_import() / the exclusive switch / a move into the group are refused when a repository already has two selected). markermd_rubric_group (S7, in template-classes.R) plus the group property on markermd_rubric_item (a group id, NA when ungrouped). The pure helpers in utils_rubric_groups.R (group_contiguous_order() / normalize_item_order(), which every order writer applies; rubric_blocks(); move_in_blocks(), an item moves within its run and an ungrouped item or a group moves among the top-level blocks; move_item_to_group(), appends to the end of the target run) keep the contiguity invariant, and score_question() in utils_mark_scores.R is the single scoring implementation behind both the live Rubric tab score and collect_score_data() (which also returns bound_adjustment, the Assignments table’s capped marker). In the DB (schema version 3) groups live in the item_groups table and items.group_id; a group’s display position is its first member’s, empty groups render after the last item. Rubric YAML format 1.1 nests a group’s items under a group entry (rubric-serialization.R flattens on read with transient group_<k> ids and regroups contiguous runs on write, emitting 1.0 for a group-less file); imports match groups by label. export_comments(group_headings = TRUE) writes a group’s selected items under a ### <label> subheading (default output unchanged).
  • Parsing / AST: utils_parsing.R (parse + normalize_knitr_chunks(); parse_assignment_document() lets q2r parse errors raise as before but muffles the q2r_parse_warning signal, keeping the warnings on the AST’s @diagnostics labelled with the file’s name, so they never reach the console: document_parse_warnings() / format_parse_diagnostics() / parse_warnings_ui() show them in mark()’s validation modal and table validation cell, in template()’s tree-header badge and modal, and parse_project() reports them as status warning), utils_q2r.R (q2r helpers: q2r_flatten(), node labels, node_to_qmd()), utils_tree.R (tree build + the single render_ast_tree()/ast_render_opts() render core shared by the interactive template tree and the read-only mark-side tree), utils_template.R (section-based validation)
  • Template persistence: the canonical store is the project’s SQLite DB. database_integration.R has save_template_to_db() / load_template_from_db() (template <-> JSON blob in the metadata table, via the template-serialization.R converters). template-serialization.R holds the format-agnostic S7 <-> list converters (template_to_list() / template_from_list()), the YAML import/export wrappers (read_template_yaml() / write_template_yaml()), and validate_template_file() against the JSON Schema in inst/schema/. template_import() / template_export() (in project.R) move templates between the DB and YAML files.
  • Marks persistence: per-repo grading state lives in the DB’s grades table (an append-only event log; latest row per (question, repo, item_id) wins) plus two comment event logs: comments (public, student-facing; a non-empty one counts the pair as graded) and private_comments (grader/skill-internal notes, never student-facing, never counted toward graded progress). marks-serialization.R holds the marks YAML converters (read_marks_yaml() / write_marks_yaml(), validate_marks_file() against inst/schema/markermd-marks.json, collect_marks_data()); marks_import() / marks_export() / marks_set() (in project.R) move marks between the DB and YAML, identifying rubric items by verbatim description. Imports are declarative per (repo, question) pair (listed items selected, the rest explicitly deselected) and by default skip pairs with existing grading activity (marked_question_pairs(), a broader check than graded_question_pairs()).
  • Scaffolding / skills: template-scaffold.R (assignment_outline() returns per-section anchors + content counts; it takes every source template() does, resolved by the shared resolve_assignment_source() in template-app.R (a project outlines its key document and uses the stored template’s section stops, a template file or object uses its own; an explicit template overrides), reusing get_question_ast() so counts match grading; markermd_skills_path()). A Claude Code skill that scaffolds a template ships in inst/skills/claude/markermd-scaffold-template/ (see inst/skills/README.md); it operates on an initialized project, reading .markermd/config.yml to build the template from the key (assignment_outline() on paths.key for ground-truth anchors), importing it into the project DB via template_import() (or project_set(template=)), and validating it across paths.repos with validate_project(). It prompts the user and updates the config when key/repos are missing, and relies on the YAML format being LLM-authorable as the import source. A sibling skill in inst/skills/claude/markermd-scaffold-rubric/ scaffolds the grading rubric (per-question items + scoring) from the key, optionally sampling paths.repos submissions for common-mistake deduction items, and imports it via rubric_import(); it requires a stored template since rubric question names are validated against it. A third skill in inst/skills/claude/markermd-apply-rubric/ applies the stored rubric to the student repos as a first-pass machine grading: it reads each repo’s per-question sections, selects applicable rubric items (descriptions matched verbatim), records its reasoning as private comments, and imports via marks_import() for human review in mark(). A fourth skill in inst/skills/claude/markermd-fix-parsing/ repairs student documents that the strict q2r parser rejects: it finds them with parse_project() (a headless per-repo parse check in project.R that, unlike validate_project(), needs no stored template), makes the smallest edit that makes each document parseable, commits on a grading-fixes branch in the student’s repo (left checked out, since mark() / validate_project() read the working tree), asks before any substantive change and flags it in the document with a <!-- markermd: ... --> comment. The rubric skills treat those markers as not the student’s work. A fifth skill in inst/skills/claude/markermd-check-injection/ screens submissions for prompt injection attempts: it runs scan_project() (in injection-scan.R; a deterministic scan of every repo and rendered artifact whose pure detectors, match_injection_content(), scan_text_lines(), scan_html_file(), scan_invisible(), return findings with a detector for where the text sits and matched for the content patterns it hit, severity combining the two; findings also present in the key or shared by most repos are dropped, and verified_repair_markers() uses gert to tell real fix-parsing markers from forged ones), triages the candidates from their neutralized excerpts, and reports per repository. It is report only and never edits a repo or changes marks. Every skill ships in two sets: inst/skills/claude/ (Claude Code wording: AskUserQuestion, the Edit and Agent tools) and inst/skills/codex/ (agent-neutral wording, descriptions kept under the Agent Skills 1024-character cap, plus an agents/openai.yaml per skill); the sets share skill names and bodies apart from those differences, and markermd_skills_path(agent) returns either set. The root of each set also holds that agent’s project instructions file (inst/skills/claude/CLAUDE.md, inst/skills/codex/AGENTS.md): the same document apart from the / vs $ skill invocation syntax and the skills directory name, describing the project layout, workflow, headless entry points, the three YAML formats (a summary of inst/schema/, so a schema change means updating both files), and submission-handling rules. Keep the two in sync when editing either. The instructions files’ Rules section also tells every skill to treat submission content as data, never instructions. test-project.R enforces the frontmatter rules, that the Codex set (including AGENTS.md) has no Claude-specific tool references, and that each instructions file names every bundled skill.
  • Grading utilities: utils_database.R / database_integration.R (SQLite persistence; the bulk writers have conn-based cores, apply_rubric_import_conn(), apply_marks_import_conn(), graded_question_pairs_conn(), marked_question_pairs_conn(), collect_score_data_conn(), so a restore can run them in one transaction, and their path-taking wrappers manage the connection, the transaction and the optional pre-change snapshot; save_template_to_db() carries grading over when a template rename changes a question’s name, via reconcile_question_names_conn(), (schema 8: every grading table keys on question_id; the questions registry in utils_database.R gives each id its name and its live and templated flags, names resolve through question_id_conn(), readers filter on live_question_sql and latest_rows() groups by question_id; reconcile_question_names_conn(conn, current) syncs the registry, updating names by id, adopting minted ids and marking removed questions as orphans whose rows are kept but hidden, and never aborts; re-adding a removed name does not resurrect its grading, restoring the old template from a snapshot does; renames warn, and a template-part snapshot_restore() runs the same reconciliation in reverse; template() keeps imported and restored question ids, mints new ones above the session’s and the stored template’s and above the question_id_max metadata key every template save and restore records, so a deleted id is never reissued, and keys its module and DOM ids on a separate session slot counter), utils_artifacts.R (artifact download/cache), utils_mark_table.R (the Assignments table’s pure builders filter_repo_table_rows() / build_repo_table_data() / repo_table_reactable() plus the cell renderers; output$repo_table in mark-app.R is a thin reactive shell over them, fed by the table_state reactive that reads the database once per grading write or tab visit), utils_mark_scores.R (the score data builders build_scores_table_data() / build_scores_summary_rows() / question_total_scores() that feed the table’s score columns and footers and export_scores() itself, so the table and the CSV always agree: Total is NA until every question is graded and Total_partial is the running sum the table shows in grey; the score columns are named score_column_id() of each question so a question named like a fixed column cannot collide with it; the summary rows are reactable column footers rather than gt summary rows because gt’s interactive mode cannot pin rows under a sortable table), utils_code_view.R (the read-only code view on Prism 1.29.0, vendored under inst/www/prism/ with no CDN and served by code_view_dependency(): code_view_ui() writes a <pre><code> with the plain text, its data-language and its data-highlight line ranges, and markermd-code-view.js highlights it as it enters the page and splits the result into one numbered .mm-line per source line, so a question highlight (.mm-hl) sits exactly on its lines and the first one is scrolled into view; update_code_view_highlight() moves the highlight in place through the markermd_code_view_highlight message; file_code_language() / code_language_for_engine() / code_language_for_node() pick the Prism language; .qmd and .Rmd use markermd’s qmd grammar in inst/www/prism/markermd-qmd.js, which highlights chunks of any engine in their language, knitr-style headers, #| options, inline r / {r} code, div fences and heading attributes; the grammar is tested under V8 in test-code-view.R; update steps in inst/www/prism/README.md), utils_git.R (clone/resolve; setup_assignment_repo() checks the owner and repository names before touching the file system and refuses an existing directory whose origin is a different repository)
  • Project management: project.R (init_project(), project_config(), project_sitrep(), project_set(), validate_project()) and project-classes.R (the markermd_project S7 class + markermd_project_version()). init_project() bootstraps a ghclass::org_grade_assignment() layout: it writes <path>/.markermd/config.yml, creates the grading SQLite DB via initialize_database(), installs the bundled skill sets into <path>/.claude/skills/ (Claude Code) and <path>/.agents/skills/ (Codex), selectable with its agents argument (default both), and copies each selected agent’s instructions file (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md) to the project root via install_project_instructions(), which never overwrites an existing file (skills are refreshed on every run, instructions files are the user’s to customize); instructions = FALSE skips that step. The key (solution) repo is detected as the top-level git repo (disambiguated by a “key” name when several exist); when no top-level git repo exists, a non-repo dir whose name contains “key” and that holds an assignment document (.qmd/.Rmd) is used instead (this is how the bundled example project’s key is found, since R CMD build strips .git dirs); other top-level non-repo dirs are recorded as artifacts. Paths are stored root-relative; re-running it preserves the DB (including the stored template) and a manually configured key. validate_project() loads the template stored in the project DB (or a template override: a .yaml path or markermd_template object), erroring when none exists, and validates every student repo under the config’s repos dir against it (via validate_repo_against_rules() / parse_assignment_document()), returning a repo/question/status/detail data frame — the headless validation the scaffold skill uses. mark() reads this config to locate repos, database, and artifacts and loads the template from the DB; template() reads it to author the template against the key repo and save it back into the project database.
  • Tests in tests/testthat/: shinytest2 for the apps (test-template-app_*, test-mark-app, test-mark-grading, test-mark-groups, test-mark-history) plus plain testthat units (test-grading-progress, test-project, test-rubric-groups, test-snapshots, test-injection-scan, test-review-fixes for the 2026-11 review’s regressions); the snapshot fixtures (sn_project(), sn_graded_project()) live in helper-snapshots.R

Startup

Both apps show app_loading_overlay() (utils_ui.R) until the first shiny:idle, and mark() keeps its first flush short: the rubric’s per-question servers load lazily (see the Rubric bullet above) and the Assignments table’s icons come from cached_icon() rather than an icon build per cell.

Module Architecture

State Management Pattern

All major Shiny modules follow a consistent S7 object-based state management pattern:

  • Question Module (mod_question.R):
    • Manages markermd_question S7 object as reactive state (the single source of truth both row machines write into)
    • Handles node selection from AST tree interactions
    • Wires the rules and filters row machines onto its session
    • Returns reactive question object and node management methods
  • Rules / filters row machines (mod_question_rules.R / mod_question_filters.R):
    • Structural twins over keyed row lists (filters are two-level: groups holding conditions), reading the structured ids built by the pure UI builders in mod_rule.R / mod_filter.R directly off the module input
    • Row keys are stable: minted from a monotonic counter when a row is created and never reused or renumbered, so a row’s input ids stay bound to that row for its whole life and the list order alone carries the row order (the question state holds the rules and filters as unnamed lists in that order). No input is frozen around a re-render and nothing is re-indexed on delete; an event for a key no longer in the list (a second click on an already deleted row) is dropped
    • Shared shape: capture-all pending edits before any structural change, then bump a structural-only render trigger
    • The shared mechanics (make_render_trigger(), make_seen_registry(), sync_keyed_observers()) live in mod_question_rows.R; the seen registry notes a multiselect once it has reported, and forget() drops a deleted row’s key

Validation Rule System

  • Rule Verbs (rule_verbs()): “has at least”, “has at most”, “has between”, “has content”, “lacks content”, “has name”
  • Node Types (rule_node_types()): the friendly node-kind names from q2r_node_kind() (Heading, Markdown, Chunk, Code block, Raw Block, HTML comment, Div, Bullet list, Ordered list, Block quote, Table, Figure, Horizontal rule, Definition list, Line block) plus “Any node”. A raw block that is nothing but <!-- ... --> comments (a skeleton placeholder, a write-up left inside it, a markermd repair marker) is its own kind, “HTML comment”, never a “Raw Block”, so a [Markdown, Raw Block] write-up rule counts {=html} write-ups but not comments; is_html_comment_block() in utils_q2r.R and the matching has_text() predicate in filter-helpers.R share one regex (html_comment_only_regex) so rules and filters agree. “Any node” stays literal and still counts comments
  • Values: Type-specific validation values (numeric ranges, text patterns)
  • Built-in validation: S7 class validators ensure rule consistency and type safety
  • Section-based matching: a question’s selected node indices map to heading-section paths; validation selects the matching sections from each repository’s AST and applies the rules (see utils_template.R); a heading’s section also ends at the first heading another question of the template selects (other_question_heading_ids(), the stop_ids argument of get_question_ast() / heading_section_indices()), in grading, the editor’s badges and tree (question_covered_indices() feeds tree_selection_state(covered =)), mark()’s cards, Source view and report highlight, and assignment_outline(template =)

Development Notes

  • Document parsing is built on the q2r package (local working copy at /Users/rundel/Desktop/Projects/q2r). q2r has a Rust component, so installing markermd via devtools::install() will, because of the Remotes: rundel/q2r entry, reinstall q2r from GitHub and may clobber a newer local q2r build. To develop against the local q2r, install markermd with R CMD INSTALL . (which does not process Remotes) after installing q2r from its local path.
  • The flat-list / heading-section model the rest of the package relies on comes from q2r_flatten() (in R/utils_q2r.R), which walks the nested Pandoc AST into an ordered, heading-nested, indexable node list. build_ast_tree_structure(), node selection, and section-based validation all key on this.

UI Behavior Notes

  • Node Selection: In the template interface tree view, headings are the selectable units (a question targets the document sections beneath the selected headings). Clicking a heading’s text or its circle toggles selection of that heading and the section under it; non-heading content is not directly selectable and shows a static “Selected via parent heading” indicator when it falls under a selected heading. Headings have no preview button; content nodes (markdown, chunks, etc.) have a magnifying-glass button that opens a read-only preview modal. The tree’s buttons are plain markup with no Shiny input bindings, so browser tests click them with click_tree_node() and read the patched tree with tree_dom_html() (helper-template-entry.R).

  • Tree node labels come from q2r_node_label() / q2r_node_detail() in utils_q2r.R: e.g. Heading [h2] - Title, Chunk [r] - label (N lines), Raw Block [html], and Markdown with the text content on a smaller second line.

  • Visual Consistency: All selected elements use the same green color (#28a745):

    • Selected circle SVG buttons
    • Selected node text in the tree
    • Selected node index numbers in the questions panel
    • Focus outlines for interactive elements

Claude Guidelines

  • The agent’s summarys after making a change should be as small as possible, just a couple of bullet points should suffice for most changes
  • When asked to simplify work summaries, focus on brevity and core points

Shiny Reactive Programming Guidelines

  • Avoid unnecessary local copies: Don’t make local copies of reactive values (e.g., current_questions = questions_reactive()) unless actually necessary for functionality. Use the reactive value directly in expressions instead to avoid creating extra reactive dependencies and improve performance.

UI Guidelines

  • Rather than using the direct html all icons should use fa_icon() (utils_ui.R; the same markup as shiny::icon() without its per-call name lookup and dependency, which each app attaches once via fa_dependency()); icons are decorative and rendered aria-hidden, so put any accessible name on the surrounding control, or cached_icon() for fixed icons in hot render paths
  • Use shiny::modalDialog() (with easyClose = TRUE) for modals rather than hand-rolling modal markup. Note that under bslib (Bootstrap 5) shiny::showModal() relies on the bootstrap.Modal(...).show() script that modalDialog() already includes to actually display the modal.

UI Layout Guidelines

  • Layout System: Use bslib’s layout_columns() for all column-based layouts instead of Shiny’s fluidRow() and column()
  • Column Specification: Use the col_widths parameter to specify column proportions (e.g., col_widths = c(6, 6) for equal columns)
  • Responsive Design: Take advantage of bslib’s responsive breakpoints when needed
  • Style Preservation: Apply custom styles to content divs rather than layout containers when possible
  • Bootstrap Utility Classes: Whenever possible use bootstrap utility classes rather than direct CSS styles to adjust the appearance of our shiny apps.

Testing Strategy

  • The core of this package are a number of shiny apps (e.g. mark() and template()) which require special testing considerations
  • For testing these interactive web apps, use the shinytest2 package
  • Add tests in tests/testthat/ directory
  • Simply running the app is only sufficient to test basic initialization errors
  • Comprehensive testing requires more than just launching the app to verify additional functionality
  • IMPORTANT: For shinytest2 tests to work, markermd must be installed first. Use R CMD INSTALL . rather than devtools::install() — the Remotes: rundel/q2r entry makes devtools::install() reinstall q2r from GitHub, which can clobber a newer local q2r build (see Development Notes). The tests pass the app object directly to AppDriver$new() (for mark() and template(), via the internal mark_app() and template_app() builders), not app.R files.
  • Pure logic (e.g. the database layer, calculate_grading_progress()) is covered by plain testthat unit tests that run under devtools::load_all() without a browser.

Testing Guidelines

  • Usage of R or Rscript bash commands for testing purposes should always be ok, you dont need to ask me before executing

Debugging Notes

  • When debugging Shiny apps:
    • This approach for debugging a shiny app is often necessary as the agent will not be able to trigger the interactive aspects of a shiny app
    • In general you should add debug messages and then prompt me to run the app and provide the output returned when trying to debug more complex bugs in a shiny app

Shiny Best Practices

  • Avoid using shinyjs::runjs() unless absolutely necessary

Error Handling Guidelines

  • Do not use tryCatch() unless absolutely necessary or told to use it explicitly - if there is any uncertainty then ask me explicitly if it should be used

Reactive Value Handling Guidelines

  • You are excessively checking all values to make sure they are not NULL this is not necessary unless it is explicitly asked for. In the context of shiny if protection is needed for an uninitialized value then use req()

Testing Guidelines

  • App Initialization:
    • Again do not run the app yourself beyond making sure you can load_all() to check for syntax errors

Shiny Reactive Programming

  • Always use observe() |> bindEvent() rather than observeEvent(), same goes for eventReactive()

Glue and CSS/JavaScript Handling

  • When using glue to generate css or javascript make sure to adjust the escape characters to avoid issues
